newsitem.title: UK: Christian Salvesen seen unveiling float plan.
newsitem.headline: Christian Salvesen seen unveiling float plan.

text.p: Scotland-based distribution and services firm Christian Salvesen is poised to unveil a long awaited plan to float its Aggreko power supply business on Monday, the Independent on Sunday said.
The firm will also hand out a special dividend to shareholders when it announces first half results.

"Sources close to the company said this weekend that Chris Masters, Salvesen's chief excutive, will only reveal the general terms of the demerger, along with the intention to pay a special dividend," the paper said.
"However, it is understood that the demerger would value Aggreko at around 400 million stg."
Christian Salvesen is forecast to disclose interim profits of around 48 to 49 million stg, up from 45 million stg from the first six months of last year.
Aggreko profits will account for about half this figure, owing in part to some unexpected contract gains in Sri Lanka and Mexico, the paper said.

The plan to float Aggreko is part of Christian Salvesen's aim to realise more shareholder value for the business after it rejected a $1.18 billion stg takeover approach from distribution group Hays in August, the paper added. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
